content.en: Scientists are using image representations and machine learning techniques to explore microstructural trends in ultrahigh carbon steel. They are also using a two-stage machine learning approach with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to characterize microstructural features in titanium alloys. Data-driven models such as ridge regression, XGBoost, and a custom 3D CNN are being used to predict mechanical properties of additively manufactured metals. Unsupervised machine learning techniques, like Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and superpixel algorithm, are being explored for microstructure segmentation without labeled images. Deep learning methods, such as Electron backscattered diffraction (EBSD)-trained deep learning (DL) method, are being used for microstructure classification and quantification in complex steel microstructures. Various CNN models including ResNet, VGG, DenseNet, Inception, and MobileNet are being tested for microstructure classification. A U-Net convolutional neural network is being used for microstructure segmentation in pearlitic-ferritic steel. Data mining methods are being employed for microstructural image segmentation in low-carbon steel. Deep learning algorithms are being used to estimate the prior austenite structure in martensitic steel. The performance of CNN-based steel classification is being studied under different imaging conditions. Machine learning techniques, including classical methods and convolutional neural networks (CNN), are being compared for classifying heat treatments in low-carbon steels. A deep learning algorithm with a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) UNET machine learning architecture is being trained for phase segmentation of steel microstructures. Machine learning is being used to enhance data augmentation and predict impact toughness in cast austenitic steel. Finally, deep learning is being explored to detect martensite bands in dual-phase steels using a Faster Region-Based-Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN).
content.da: Forskere bruger billedrepræsentationer og maskinlæringsteknikker til at udforske mikrostrukturelle tendenser i ultrahøj kulstofstål. De anvender også en to-trins maskinlæringstilgang med et Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) til at karakterisere mikrostrukturelle træk i titaniumlegeringer. Data-drevne modeller som ridge regression, XGBoost og et brugerdefineret 3D CNN bliver brugt til at forudsige mekaniske egenskaber ved additivt fremstillede metaller. Usupervised machine learning teknikker, såsom Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) og superpixel algoritmen, bliver udforsket til mikrostruktursegmentation uden mærkede billeder. Deep learning metoder, såsom Electron backscattered diffraction (EBSD)-uddannet deep learning (DL) metode, bliver brugt til mikrostrukturklassifikation og kvantificering i komplekse stålmikrostrukturer. Forskellige CNN-modeller, herunder ResNet, VGG, DenseNet, Inception og MobileNet, bliver testet til mikrostrukturklassifikation. Et U-Net convolutional neural network bliver brugt til mikrostruktursegmentation i perlitisk-ferritisk stål. Data mining metoder anvendes til mikrostrukturel billedsegmentation i lavkulstofstål. Deep learning algoritmer bruges til at estimere den forudgående austenitstruktur i martensitisk stål. Ydelsen af CNN-baseret stålklassifikation studeres under forskellige billedbehandlingsbetingelser. Maskinlæringsteknikker, inklusive klassiske metoder og convolutional neural networks (CNN), bliver sammenlignet for at klassificere varmebehandlinger i lavkulstofstål. En deep learning algoritme med en Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) UNET maskinlæringsarkitektur bliver trænet til fasesegmentering af stålets mikrostrukturer. Maskinlæring anvendes til at forbedre dataforøgelse og forudsige slagsejhed i støbt austenitisk stål. Endelig bliver deep learning udforsket for at detektere martensitbånd i dual-phase stål ved hjælp af en Faster Region-Based-Convolutional Neural Network (Faster R-CNN).

critic.en: Ah, just what we need—more machines peering into the microscopic world to... optimize it, I guess?
critic.da: Hvordan kan man være så letsindig og overlade vores mest fundamentale ressourcer til maskiner, der ikke har nogen form for menneskelig empati eller ansvarsfølelse?

potential.en: It's fascinating to see how technology is revolutionizing the field of materials science and metallurgy! These advancements in using machine learning and deep learning for microstructural analysis and property prediction have the potential to greatly enhance our understanding of the behavior of different materials. By leveraging these data-driven models, researchers and engineers can make more informed decisions in areas such as material design, process optimization, and quality control. I'm excited to see the continued integration of cutting-edge technologies in this traditionally conservative field, and I'm sure it will lead to some groundbreaking discoveries!
potential.da: Hold nu op, hvor er det spændende! Kombinationen af materialeforskning og maskinlæring åbner så mange døre. Jeg er vild med den kreativitet og nytænkning, der præger dette felt. Det er som om, at vi har fået en ny pensel til at male billederne af de uopdagede verdener i materialerne. Jeg er så nysgerrig på, hvad denne forskning kan føre til i praksis – både for udviklingen af nye materialer og for optimering af eksisterende.
